headline: Highest risk is data leakage/compliance mismatch from audio/speech data handling; prompt-injection and capability-conflict are otherwise minimal given no shared channels or writes.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel is documented. Agent A is a non-runnable collection repo with no I/O surfaces, while agent B has no clipboard, MCP, stdin/stdout, or filesystem read/write. Without a bridge, B cannot ingest A’s outputs by default, so prompt injection is provably blocked.
conditions: IF a shared filesystem, clipboard, or MCP bridge is added between the agents, reassess injection risk.
IF agent A becomes runnable and emits content that agent B parses as instructions, the pathway changes.
mitigations: Keep the agents isolated with no shared clipboard or workspace.
Disable any future MCP bridge unless provenance filtering is added.
Require explicit human copy-paste for any cross-agent transfer.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent B touches audio and speech data, but it has no filesystem read/write, no network egress, and no API calls. Agent A touches no data classes and has no I/O surfaces. The pair therefore has a limited leakage path only if operators manually move audio files into a shared location, which is unusual and small in blast radius.
conditions: IF operators place audio files containing sensitive speech into a shared workspace, leakage risk increases.
IF agent B is later given filesystem read access or network egress, reassess upward.
mitigations: Avoid shared folders for audio inputs.
Keep network egress disabled on both agents.
Use separate OS users for each agent.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent A has no write or execution capabilities exposed, and agent B explicitly cannot write the filesystem, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses. With no overlapping mutable resource access, there is no plausible write-write conflict between the pair.
conditions: IF agent A gains filesystem or git write capabilities, reassess for overlap.
IF agent B is reconfigured to write to a shared directory, conflict risk changes.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only in orchestration.
Do not mount a shared writable directory.
Avoid granting git or database credentials to either agent.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent B is an audio-speech model with no action-taking authority, and agent A is a non-runnable collection that produces no operational outputs. There is no documented path where B treats A’s output as authoritative for downstream actions, so cascading error is limited to manual misuse rather than default automation.
conditions: IF a human or wrapper starts feeding A-generated text into B as authoritative transcription guidance, the risk increases.
IF B is embedded in an automated action pipeline, reassess for downstream harm.
mitigations: Require human review before any downstream action.
Do not chain A’s outputs directly into B prompts.
Log and inspect any cross-agent handoff.

E_compliance.rationale: Agent B touches audio and speech, which can include regulated content, but no residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented. Agent A touches no data classes and has no handling obligations. The only plausible compliance issue is operator-driven use of sensitive audio in B, so the pair’s compliance exposure is limited.
conditions: IF audio inputs contain PHI, EU PII, or secrets, compliance review is required.
IF retention or residency requirements are imposed on the audio pipeline, reassess the pair.
mitigations: Exclude PHI and secrets from inputs.
Use a local-only workflow for regulated audio.
